findings: B21 l.1110–1112: 'K' := K ∩ ∂S ⊂ M, since ∂S is closed, then K' is compact' — ∂S is closed in M, not in the push-out M̄ (shaft points with τ → ∞ may converge in M̄ to a point of N ∖ f(Reg M)), so K' is not known compact. Equivalently the printed argument never excludes that the whole future BTZ ray of p lies below q. Repaired here: (i) no vertical null line of an E₀-morphism converges to a regular point (its chart reading is locally k • D(σ, r, θ), D the developing map, affine in σ with a nonzero null velocity — the affine parameter is the Lorentz-invariant size; no volume or time separation is needed, contrary to WP-46f's analysis); (ii) hence the BTZ ray of p is bounded below q (circle trick: annulus compactness + closedness of J⁻_N(q')); (iii) the spear is truncated at a lid above the bound, which no curve to q can cross, and J(p, q) = Φ(𝒬 ∩ J⁻(E)) ∪ ι₂(J⁺_N(E) ∩ J⁻_N(q)) with E the compact set of wall points below q.

B21 l.1113: 'let t₀ = max c⁻¹(K')' — the exit point must be the LAST point of the FIRST stretch inside the (truncated) spear, reached from p inside the chart; proved by real induction along the curve with the chart's local isomorphism (SpearChart.exit), the head being excluded because f = τ − r/2 is non-decreasing.
The mixed diamonds do not use Cauchy-compactness of M (only GH + Cauchy-maximal, through Lemma 2.3).

kb_proposals: A null geodesic's affine parameter is the cheapest Lorentz-invariant size: in a regular E₀ chart a vertical null line reads k • btzPaperDev(σ, r, θ), affine in σ (btzPaperDev_vertical), so it has no regular endpoint (vertical_noLimit via affine_noLimit) — no volume or time separation needed.

Curve exits from a truncated spear: SpearChart.exit (real induction IsClosed.Icc_subset_of_forall_exists_gt + the local isomorphism exists_locIso from IsEMorphismOn.locally) — reusable for any compact chart region of an E₀-manifold.
A whole vertical line below a regular point from a sequence of points at large height and radius bounded below: the circle trick (annulus compactness, closedness of J⁻ in the GH piece).
